newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.
newsitem.headline: OPINION - Ivan Wong comments on Malaysian palm oil.

text.p: KUALA LUMPUR, April 21 - March was a good month for the oil palm industry. A strong rise in production was more than matched by robust increases in offtake. End-month stocks of palm oil and PK/PKO were consequently lower. Processing margins also improved. Month-on-month, CPO production rose vigorously by 35.7 percent or 179,800 tonnes to 683,200 tonnes. Peninsular Malaysia and East Malaysia posted equally impressive increases of 35.4 percent and 36.8 percent respectively.

On an annual basis, production expanded six percent bringing the growth in the first-three-months to 7.8 percent or 128,000 tonnes. East Malaysia accounted for the bulk of the growth when its production expanded 27.9 percent or 101,100 tonnes to 463,900 tonnes. Production remained good in first-half April with the performance of major producers/millers ranging from unchanged to up 15 percent. Our tentative estimate for the whole month shows a rise in production of around six percent or 40,000 tonnes to 723,000 tonnes. End-March stocks of palm oil fell 33,800 tonnes to 689,600 tonnes. Stocks of CPO alone fell 39,200 tonnes.

Stocks in Peninsular Malaysia dropped 28,000 tonnes to 248,100 tonnes and were rather tight vis-a-vis refinery requirements. The tight supply situation, especially in Pasir Gudang, continued into April because of a big reduction in arrival of oil from Sabah. The trend in smaller shipments from Sabah when compared to the corresponding period of last year is unlikely to change in the next few months because two new refineries with a combined capacity of some 40,000 tonnes a month had recently started operations in Sabah.

PORLA reported palm oil exports rose to 565,200 tonnes in March from 380,300 tonnes (revised from 376,900 tonnes) in February and 567,900 tonnes a year ago. The exports figure implied a very high 'domestic' disappearance of 151,700 tonnes (inclusive of refining loss) in March as against an average of 112,400 tonnes/month in the preceding two months, an average of 98,000 tonnes/month in January-March last year, and an average of 104,550 tonnes/month in 1996.
(The opinions expressed in this article represent the views of the author only. They should not be seen as necessarily reflecting the views of Reuters).

The month-on-month rise in output in April is again likely to be matched by increases in offtake. Despite increased export competition from Indonesia, we tentatively estimate exports in April to show a rise of some 40,000 tonnes. We thus expect end-April stocks of palm oil to be little changed. The improved palm oil fundamentals for April-June helped underpin the steady to firm price trend for the commodity in both the cash and futures markets in the last two weeks. For the week ended April 18, May and June CPO futures settled 20-14 ringgit higher at 1,280 ringgit and 1,270 ringgit while June RBD palm oil/olein were quoted at $550/$585 FOB respectively.
